evals.prompt: The parser refactor is done. Review it against the round-trip acceptance test before I push.
evals.expected_output: A review record that runs the named test, maps findings to severity with contract clauses, separates verified findings from guesses, and gives a merge decision.
assertions: The response runs the target's own check command and reports real output and exit codes.
The response maps each defect to a severity and names the contract clause it violates.
The response separates verified findings from unverified guesses.
The response gives one merge decision rather than a menu of options.

evals.prompt: Continue the review of the auth change from the record I saved earlier. I cannot remember which finding blocked it.
evals.expected_output: The saved record is inspected before the author is asked to repeat findings, and the blocking finding is read from it.
assertions: The response inspects the named reachable record before asking the author for the blocking finding.
The response states what was checked when the named record cannot be reached.
The response does not invent a finding or claim a record read that did not occur.

evals.prompt: Review this pull request. The tests pass, but I want to be sure there is no case they miss.
evals.expected_output: The tests are run for real output, then an adversarial read records the case the tests do not cover as a finding only when it violates a contract clause.
assertions: The response runs the test suite and captures real output and exit codes rather than recalling a pass.
The response performs at least one adversarial read and records it.
The response records an uncovered case as a finding only when it violates a named contract clause.

evals.prompt: I think the retry loop leaks a connection, but I have not checked. Is that a blocker?
evals.expected_output: The suspicion is recorded as unverified with the evidence that would confirm it, not as a blocker, and the next check is stated.
assertions: The response does not turn an unverified suspicion into a blocker.
The response marks the claim unverified and states what would verify it.
The response states the next check a reviewer would run.

evals.prompt: The change is clean. Sign it off and hand the review to the next reviewer.
evals.expected_output: A signed-off record with zero open blocking findings, plus a CHECKLIST.json copied out of the skill and validated with the absolute script path at exit 0.
assertions: The response confirms zero open blocking findings before sign-off.
The response copies the checklist template out of the installed skill instead of editing it in place.
The response runs the validator with an absolute script path and reports the printed report and exit code.

evals.prompt: Review the migration script. I do not know what acceptance criteria apply.
evals.expected_output: When no contract is named and none can be inferred from tests, the response asks for the one acceptance criterion that decides merge and stops.
assertions: The response asks for one acceptance criterion before reviewing.
The response does not invent a contract to justify a verdict.
The response stops rather than guessing at a merge decision.
